articles.title: 42AI Raises $62.5M Seed for a World Model That Predicts Human Behavior
articles.snippet: 42AI Raises $62.5M Seed for a World Model That Predicts Human Behavior Wowtale
articles.text:
Today’s AI can read, write and generate images, but predicting what a person will do in an unfamiliar situation is a different problem. Human behavior is never fixed. It can only be described in probabilities, and two people react differently to the same news. A startup that wants to predict those reactions has just come out of stealth.
42AI , an Israeli-American startup, said on Nov. 2 that it has secured $62.5 million in seed funding. It is not a conventional outside round. CEO Amit Gal-Or told TechCrunch the money came from the founders and Infinity Group over three years. Infinity Group is an Israeli investment group founded by Amit’s father, Amir Gal-Or. The company plans to raise outside capital later. Its website describes 42AI as a U.S.-Israeli “frontier AI lab” born from more than a decade of Infinity Group research and cites an initial investment of $15 million, so how that figure relates to $62.5 million is unclear.
42AI calls its product a “Behavioral World Model.” A world model is an AI system that simulates how the world will change, and it is usually applied to robots and self-driving cars that must anticipate the physical world. 42AI applies the idea to people instead. It estimates what a person would decide in a situation they have never faced, as probabilities across the possible choices. The company says the model simulates and predicts how people and AI agents behave “in volatile, unprecedented environments.”
It works in two stages. Behavioral observations are first converted into a mathematical representation of a person’s tendencies. A transformer-based world model then uses that representation to output the probability of each decision in a given situation. A separate language model only explains which traits and context drove the prediction. The company says the world model responds in 1 to 10 milliseconds and its “Large Behavior Model” in 2 to 12 milliseconds. Its site says the technology rests on a “behavioral ontology,” a structured map of concepts and relationships linking individual traits, situations, world events and the model.
Training data comes in three tiers. In research it used psychological assessments of thousands of people plus government and biobank datasets covering more than 2 million people, and for customers it uses client data covering about 30 million people. The company says it combined psychology, neuroscience and genetics research over three years. The research is summarized in a February paper on high-precision behavioral prediction for strategic forecasting. The paper fine-tuned Meta’s Llama 3.1 8B on trait profiles from psychological testing to predict individuals’ strategic choices, and reported that predictions improved as more trait dimensions were added. The training data is not public, and there has been no independent validation.
The first market is brokerages. The company says its system lets a brokerage forecast each client’s trades up to 24 hours ahead by security, direction and size, so the firm can see its risk exposure before volatility hits, hedge (take offsetting positions to limit losses), and manage liquidity and margin. Gal-Or says 10 large brokerages use it and that revenue is in the seven figures. One brokerage reportedly made about $30 million in gains from dynamic hedging. Pricing is either a flat fee or a share of the value the platform creates. Customer names have not been disclosed.

Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital co-lead funding for autonomous AI platform that continuously builds, tests and improves digital experiences
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coframe, the company building websites, landing pages, and ads that continuously generate, test and improve themselves, today announced it has raised $35 million in total funding, including a $25 million Series A co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital, with participation from leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.
Continue Reading
Coframe AI Raises $35 Million to Build the "Living Internet" led by Khosla Ventures
Post this
Josh Payne, CEO & Founder of Coframe, previously co-founded Autograph with Tom Brady that reached $2B+
Founder and CEO Josh Payne calls the company's vision "the living internet." Instead of every visitor seeing the same static website, Coframe plugs into a company's website or advertising campaigns and continuously generates, tests and deploys new variations, personalizing what each visitor sees and improving performance in real time. Apps, email, and other digital experiences are next on the roadmap.
Behind it is a specialized transformer model trained on user interactions, and a team of AI agents: a strategist, a designer, a software engineer, a QA specialist, and a data scientist, that can ideate, build, test and optimize hundreds of website and ad variations in minutes.
Coframe has generated more than $300 million in incremental revenue for its customers, including conversion rate increases of 158% for Dropbox, 410% for Replit, and 60% for Cash App. And the results come fast: for one Fortune 500 customer, Coframe launched dozens of variations and delivered a 70% lift in conversion within 30 days of contract signature. Across its customer base, which includes Dropbox, BCG, Block, Backcountry, Sur La Table, and other leading brands, conversion rates have improved by more than 20% on average.
At Dropbox, an experiment that previously required four weeks of engineering, design, and QA work was built and deployed in 30 minutes with Coframe. Across thousands of variants, the platform has achieved a 39% experiment win rate, more than three times the industry average, while increasing customers' testing velocity ten times or more.
"We're building an internet that improves itself," said Josh Payne, founder and CEO of Coframe. "A digital experience should understand what it is trying to accomplish, adapt to the person interacting with it and learn from every result. Instead of waiting months for the next redesign, companies should have websites and applications that get better every day."
"For decades, the web has been frozen in place, showing every visitor essentially the same page," said Vinod Khosla, founder of Khosla Ventures. "Coframe is building the living internet, where two people can visit the same website and have completely different experiences, personalized to who they are and what they need. These interfaces continuously learn and improve themselves. This is a huge leap beyond traditional A/B testing and the next iteration of the internet."

Coframe Raises $25M Series A, Bringing Total Funding to $35M
Published
November 9, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Coframe announced on November 9, 2026 that it had raised $35 million in total funding, including a $25 million Series A co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital, according to its funding release .
Leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind also participated in the round, while Nat Friedman and Antler are listed among Coframe’s broader backers. Josh Payne founded the company in 2023. Coframe is developing websites, landing pages and advertisements that generate, test and improve variations of themselves rather than remaining static between redesigns.
Payne calls the underlying vision the living internet. “A digital experience should understand what it is trying to accomplish, adapt to the person interacting with it and learn from every result,” he said. The approach shifts website work from periodic redesigns toward ongoing experiments whose results inform subsequent changes.
How Coframe Automates Website Experiments
The system assigns AI agents to strategy, design, software engineering, quality assurance and data analysis. Coframe says they can ideate, build, test and optimize hundreds of website and advertising variations in minutes. Its proprietary user-behavior model is trained on interactions across hundreds of millions of sessions each month, allowing results from one experiment to inform later ones.
Coframe’s product overview describes a workflow that scores and ranks proposed experiments by expected conversion and revenue impact. The system then creates on-brand interfaces, writes code and runs automated quality assurance across devices. Customers approve variations before they go live. Installation uses a JavaScript snippet, and Coframe can operate alongside existing testing tools.
Company-Reported Customer Results
Coframe reports more than $300 million in incremental revenue generated for customers and an average conversion-rate improvement above 20% across a customer base that includes Dropbox , BCG, Block, Backcountry and Sur La Table. The revenue figure measures customer gains, not Coframe’s own sales.
Coframe reports a 158% conversion lift for Dropbox over six months and a 39% experiment win rate across thousands of variants. At Dropbox, an experiment that previously required four weeks of engineering, design and quality-assurance work was built and deployed in 30 minutes. Together, the figures present the company’s case that automating production and analysis can increase both the pace and the outcome of experimentation.
OpenAI Work and Agent-Facing Pages
Coframe says it is also working with OpenAI on the ChatGPT ads offering, aiming to let customers optimize an advertisement and its landing page as one continuously learning experience. The work builds on an earlier collaboration to train a specialized model for generating on-brand code and creative assets.
OpenAI’s October 1, 2024 vision fine-tuning announcement provides an example of that earlier work. OpenAI reported that Coframe fine-tuned GPT-4o with images and code, producing a 26% improvement in generating websites with consistent visual style and correct layout compared with base GPT-4o. That project focused on generating digital content; Coframe’s newly described user-behavior model instead learns from interactions across digital experiences.

Midstream Health Raises $20M Series A to Strengthen the Financial Sustainability of America’s Health Systems
AI Platform Now Optimizes Financial Decision-Making Across Health Systems Representing More Than $100 Billion in Annual Operating Expenses and 250 Hospitals
Midstream Health , the autonomous financial operations platform for health systems, today announced a $20 million Series A as it expands across a customer network representing more than $100 billion in annual operating expenses and over 250 hospitals nationwide. Midstream helps these institutions find and recover margin across both revenue and cost, strengthening the financial capacity required to continue investing in care and serving their communities.
The financing round was led by Valtruis with continued participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Foundry, and CommonSpirit Ventures, bringing Midstream’s total funding to $29.2 million. Fairview Health Services and Keck Medicine of USC are among the newest health systems to join the platform, alongside CommonSpirit Health, Mount Sinai Health System and Houston Methodist.
This announcement comes as health systems are facing a financial sustainability crisis, fighting to protect razor-thin margins. More than 110 rural hospitals have closed over the past 20 years, and another 720 — representing roughly a third of all rural hospitals — are at risk of closure. Much of what’s slipping away is money health systems have already earned, buried in their own contracts and spend. Recovering that margin is about more than improving the bottom line; it gives health systems greater capacity to invest in care, serve their communities, and deliver on the mission their patients depend on.
“In this environment, health systems need solutions that can improve their financial position quickly,” said Mike Spadafore, Managing Director of Valtruis…

Funding
geniosAI Raises $19.1M in Combined Seed and Series A Funding
Published
November 9, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Financial intelligence startup geniosAI announced on November 9, 2026 that it had raised $19.1 million in combined seed and Series A funding and emerged from stealth. FactSet led the Series A, with Zoom and General Catalyst also investing as geniosAI brings products to market for corporate finance and investment teams.
The San Jose, California, company is co-founded and led by chief executive Prabhdeep Singh. Its products are aimed at the office of the CFO and at investment professionals on both the buy side and sell side. geniosAI says finance and investment teams at Fortune 500 global banks and technology companies already use the platform for earnings preparation, including peer and analyst-expectation comparisons, identifying notable items and anticipating questions from analysts.
A Platform Built for Review
geniosAI says its platform is designed to preserve institutional context across investment research and modeling assignments, with reasoning shown and figures linked to their sources. Singh described the mechanism as a persistent record of the work: “geniosAI keeps the sources, calculations, assumptions, and review decisions attached to the work, so the institution can trace every number, challenge it, and build on it the next time.”
Examples Across Finance Workflows
On geniosAI’s website , the company divides its illustrated agent roles into two groups. System 1 is described as quick, certain and narrow, with a Junior Analyst, Controller and Accountant; System 2 is slow, thorough and deep, with a Chief of Staff, Deep Researcher and Senior Reviewer. Both groups answer to the user.
In an office-of-the-CFO example, a Controller opens the ledger, an Accountant reconciles 412 lines, the Controller flags two variances and a Chief of Staff drafts a board summary. An investment-banking workflow shows a Deep Researcher reading new guidance, a Junior Analyst changing three drivers and rebuilding the model, and a Senior Reviewer checking it against the previous version. Another example follows a requested figure back to its filing, replays the calculation and identifies who produced it.
Strategic Backers and Their Roles
FactSet is also geniosAI’s strategic partner. CEO Sanoke Viswanathan said the partnership combines his company’s data with geniosAI’s traceable analysis to help teams move from insight to decision. Zoom Chief Strategy Officer Abhisht Arora said the investment fits Zoom’s focus on moving work from conversation to completion and builds on its work with finance teams and financial institutions.
General Catalyst managing director Madhu Namburi said the larger opportunity is a higher, more consistent level of intelligence across an organization, with judgment remaining with the business. That thesis also frames the central question for geniosAI’s market entry: whether source tracing and retained context can become embedded in recurring institutional work, making analysis easier to review and reuse across teams.
